oligos.notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] Name given EXACTLY as 'nusinersen' so the assembler merges this into the existing CNS012 entry rather than creating a duplicate. Every design field here was read out of the label SPL fetched this session (DailyMed setid dd70cd5f-b0fc-4ba4-a5ea-89a34778bd94, version 21, effectiveTime 20260331). Section 11 DESCRIPTION states verbatim: 'Nusinersen is a modified antisense oligonucleotide, where the 2'-hydroxy groups of the ribofuranosyl rings are replaced with 2'-O-2-methoxyethyl groups and the phosphate linkages are replaced with phosphorothioate linkages. Nusinersen binds to a specific sequence in the intron downstream of exon 7 of the SMN2 transcript.' Uniform 2'-MOE with no DNA gap -> gapmer_design=NA, oligo_class=splice_switching_ASO. length_nt=18 and ps_count=17 are ARITHMETIC from the molecular formula printed in the same section, C234H323N61O128P17S17Na17: P17 = 17 internucleotide linkages = 18 nucleotides; S17 = 17 phosphorothioates = every linkage, hence full_PS. MW 7501.0 daltons. These are derived from a fetched document, not recalled. sequence_5to3=TBD because section 11 renders the structure only as a 'Structural Formula' image and prints no base string; the existing CNS012 row already carries the sequence from the WHO INN list and EMA EPAR and should be preferred on merge. THE LABEL NOW CARRIES TWO APPROVED REGIMENS (Table 1, sec 2.1): Low Dose Regimen = four 12 mg loading doses (three at 14-day intervals, fourth 30 days later) then 12 mg every 4 months; High Dose Regimen = two 50 mg loading doses 14 days apart then 28 mg every 4 months. Three vial strengths are supplied: 12 mg/5 mL, 28 mg/5 mL, 50 mg/5 mL (sec 11 and sec 3).

oligos.oligo_name: ASO class - SafeSense human adverse event atlas (112 ASOs)
oligos.indication: mixed - 112 ASO therapeutics spanning neurodegenerative, neurodevelopmental, systemic, ophthalmic and oncologic indications
oligos.developer: Sheba Medical Center / Tel Aviv University with the preclinical working group of the N=1 Collaborative (N1C)
oligos.notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] CLASS-LEVEL AGGREGATE ENTRY, not a single molecule - mirrors the existing class_review convention used by CNS281/CNS308/CNS490/CNS491. Represents the SafeSense atlas: 41,730 treated patients across 112 ASO treatments, 42,092 reported adverse events comprising 1,734 distinct AE terms, of which 7,072 (16.8%) were classified as severe; AEs were reported for 87 treatments and 58 treatments had documented severe AEs. Built from 616 included records (323 peer-reviewed articles, 209 clinical trial registry records, 62 gray literature sources, 13 prescribing information documents, 9 FAERS records) screened from 3,396 identified; 246 sources provided evaluable safety information. Database last updated February 2026. backbone_chemistry=mixed and gapmer_design=NA because the atlas deliberately spans both gapmer and fully-modified (FM) architectures and both PS-only and mixed PO/PS backbones - those contrasts are the substance of the paper. conjugate=other because both GalNAc-conjugated and unconjugated systemic ASOs are included. length_nt=TBD: the paper reports only that lengths cluster around ~20 nt (Figure S2A), never a single value. WARNING FOR THE ASSEMBLER: this is an AGGREGATOR of primary sources, and its 41,730-patient cohort already contains nusinersen (described in the paper as contributing 'a substantial proportion of treated participants'), tofersen, tominersen and n-of-1 ASOs that this dataset already holds from primary sources. No per-oligo AE rate from this atlas has been filed. Only cross-programme structure-toxicity associations are filed, and every one of them is flagged.

measurements.source_table: Figure 4B panel BII (radar plot, intrathecal administration only) and Figure 4A panel AI (WLS coefficient plot), with the Results subsection 'Gapmer ASOs are associated with higher adverse event rates than fully modified ASOs'
measurements.notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] HEADLINE CNS FINDING OF THE ATLAS. Paper states verbatim: 'Radar-based analyses revealed broadly elevated AE rates across multiple clinical domains among gapmers, particularly within procedure-related and neurologic categories (Figure 4B)' and 'Within the i.t. subgroup, gapmers exhibited substantially higher AE rates than FM ASOs across multiple AE categories, including pronounced differences in procedure-related and neurologic domains (Figure 4BII), with corresponding WLS models demonstrating significant effect estimates.' readout_value=TBD BECAUSE THE MAGNITUDE IS PRESENTED ONLY AS A RADAR PLOT AND A COEFFICIENT PLOT - no numeric neurologic AE rate, numerator or per-category denominator is printed anywhere in the text, tables or supplementary tables (S1 is a source list, S2 the AE dictionary, S3 ASO metadata). Denominator available only at atlas level: 41,730 treated patients across 112 ASO treatments. Method is exposure-weighted weighted-least-squares regression at treatment level, so the unit of analysis is the ASO programme, not the patient. AUTHORS' OWN CAVEAT, which must travel with this row: 'Because nusinersen accounts for a substantial proportion of treated participants and is concentrated within the FM, 2'-MOE, and i.t. strata' they ran leave-one-out and equal-ASO-weighted sensitivity analyses, and conclude 'the gapmer-FM comparison is best viewed as an exposure-weighted clinical safety association rather than a definitive agent-independent class effect.' Graded 1, not 2: the readout is an aggregate clinical AE-category rate with no severity-resolved CNS event definition, no neuronal-injury biomarker and no imaging, so nothing in the rubric's grade-2 band (sustained neuroinflammation, treatment-emergent NfL rise, ventriculomegaly, or a specific clinically significant neurologic AE) is actually demonstrated. Severe-AE analyses were directionally consistent but were not resolved to the neurologic domain. RESTATES PRIMARY ROWS: this association is computed over a cohort that already includes nusinersen, tofersen, tominersen and n-of-1 ASOs held in this dataset from primary sources - it is a re-analysis of overlapping evidence, not independent evidence, and its patients must never be added to the per-oligo rows. grade_provisional

measurements.source_table: Figure 5B panels BI and BII (WLS regression, LNA vs 2'-MOE, stratified by route) and Figure 5A, with the Results subsection 'Sugar chemistry influences ASO safety profiles'
measurements.notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] SUGAR-CHEMISTRY CONTRAST WITH A CNS-RELEVANT ROUTE STRATIFICATION. Paper states verbatim: 'Across all treatments, LNA-modified ASOs exhibited significantly higher overall AE rates compared with 2'-MOE-modified ASOs. This difference persisted after stratification by administration route and after inclusion or exclusion of N-of-1 studies' and 'the strongest differences between LNA and 2'-MOE were observed within i.t. administration.' On the neurologic domain specifically the paper says of Figure 5A: 'Among all classes, phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomers (PMO) and 2'-MOE-modified ASOs exhibited the lowest overall AE rates... In contrast, higher AE burdens were observed for LNA and other sugar chemistries. These differences were particularly evident within general, infections, and neurologic AE categories.' The authors further report the effect survives restriction to gapmers only (Figure 5AII), i.e. sugar chemistry contributes independently of architecture. readout_value=TBD - effect sizes are drawn as WLS coefficient plots with confidence intervals; no numeric AE rate, count or per-chemistry denominator is printed in the text. Significance markers on Figure 5B are given only as asterisk bands (**p<0.01, ***p<0.001, ****p<0.0001) and no exact p-value for the LNA/2'-MOE comparison appears in the text. Graded 1 for the same reason as TMP_dca_m3: an aggregate AE-category association, not a demonstrated CNS injury. RESTATES PRIMARY ROWS: the 2'-MOE intrathecal stratum is dominated by nusinersen, which this dataset already holds from the FDA label, the EMA EPAR and NCT02193074/NCT02292537/NCT04089566; the LNA stratum overlaps tominersen and other programmes already held. Not independent evidence. grade_provisional

measurements.source_table: Figure 6C (accumulated AE rates across clinical groups for 2'-MOE-modified treatments stratified by backbone, log1p scale) and Figure 6A, with the Results subsection 'Backbone composition and AE patterns'
measurements.notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] BACKBONE CONTRAST. Paper states verbatim, after restricting to 2'-MOE-modified gapmer ASOs to reduce confounding by sugar chemistry: 'Within this subset, AE category patterns remained generally consistent between backbone configurations, with slightly higher representation of several AE categories observed in PS-only treatments. However, neurologic and procedure-related AE categories remained relatively more pronounced in PO/PS-modified ASOs (Figure 6C).' Across all treatments PO/PS configurations were associated with higher overall AE rates than PS-only designs. delivery_method=TBD because Figure 6C is not stratified by route. readout_value=TBD - Figure 6C is a log1p-transformed bar plot with no printed values, counts or denominators. THIS IS THE WEAKEST OF THE THREE STRUCTURE-TOXICITY ROWS AND SHOULD BE TREATED AS HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING. The authors themselves temper it twice: when restricted to severe AEs 'this association was less evident, with attenuated effect estimates and less consistent statistical significance across strata... the PO/PS-associated signal appears to primarily reflect overall reported AE frequency or non-severe tolerability burden rather than a consistent increase in severe toxicity'; and they conclude the backbone comparison shows 'relatively modest and context-dependent differences in AE patterns'. Note the direction here runs OPPOSITE to the preclinical literature the same paper cites (reference 29/30, reduced-PS and mixed-backbone designs improving tolerability for a C9ORF72 ASO), which the authors attribute to confounding by chemistry, indication, route and candidate selection plus survivorship - 'PS-related toxicities may be eliminated before clinical testing, resulting in a clinical dataset enriched for better-tolerated ASOs.' A reviewer should not read this row as evidence that PO/PS backbones are more neurotoxic. Graded 1 provisionally. RESTATES PRIMARY ROWS: computed over programmes already in this dataset. grade_provisional

measurements.source_table: Figure 4C (scatterplot of ASO length vs mean safety rate with linear regression and 95% CI) and Figure S2B (length bins), with the Results subsection 'ASO length is not associated with AE burden'
measurements.notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] GRADE 0 NEGATIVE / NULL-ASSOCIATION ROW - recorded because the rubric treats negatives as first-class. Paper states verbatim: 'When analyzed as a continuous variable, nucleotide length demonstrated no significant association with mean AE ratio, with both Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses indicating weak and non-significant relationships (Figure 4C)' and, after binning into 19 nt or fewer, 20-24 nt, and 25 nt or more, 'Comparative analyses revealed no statistically significant differences in AE ratios across length categories (Figure S2B), as confirmed by both parametric and non-parametric tests.' readout_value=TBD and no correlation coefficient or p-value is printed in the text - only the qualitative statement and the figures. Lengths cluster around ~20 nt (Figure S2A), so the tested range is narrow and the null is correspondingly weak; absence of an association over a narrow range is not evidence of absence over a wide one. is_cns_specific=FALSE because this analysis is over ALL AEs across all routes, not a CNS-compartment readout - it is filed as a design-predictor negative, not as a CNS measurement, and must not be counted as a CNS observation. The authors read the null as support for a structural rather than hybridization-driven model of toxicity: 'If toxicity were predominantly mediated by hybridization-dependent off-target effects, longer ASOs would be expected to demonstrate improved specificity and reduced AE burden - a trend that was not observed.' RESTATES PRIMARY ROWS: aggregate over programmes already held. grade_provisional

measurements.effect_vs_control: neurologic_terms_reported_but_nonspecific (headache, dizziness, fall); authors conclude no meaningful CNS exposure
measurements.source_table: Figure 7C (accumulated prevalence of neurologic AE terms following systemic i.v. and s.c. administration), with the Results subsection 'Cross-compartment AE patterns suggest limited peripheral toxicity after i.t. delivery and limited CNS toxicity after systemic delivery'
measurements.notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] GRADE 0 CROSS-COMPARTMENT NEGATIVE CONTROL - a systemically dosed population with no evidence of CNS exposure, exactly the negative-comparator case the schema describes for is_cns_specific=FALSE. Paper states verbatim: 'Although neurologic events were reported, the most common terms included headache, dizziness, and fall, events that are relatively nonspecific and not necessarily indicative of direct CNS toxicity. Additional reported events, such as neuropathy, may reflect peripheral nervous system involvement rather than central exposure' and concludes 'neurologic AEs observed with systemic administration were predominantly nonspecific and do not suggest meaningful CNS exposure.' readout_value=TBD: Figure 7C shows accumulated prevalence per term but no value, count or denominator is printed in the text. The three named terms - headache, dizziness, fall - are recorded here rather than as three separate rows because the paper gives no per-term rate, and splitting one unquantified statement into three rows would manufacture volume without adding evidence. The authors offer a mechanistic reading in the Discussion: headache 'may reflect a nonspecific systemic tolerability signal, often a part of flu-like symptoms and injection/infusion reactions', and neuropathy is 'plausibly linked to peripheral sensory neuron (ganglion/DRG) exposure'. They also flag one genuine counterexample outside this dataset - the s.c. ASO RGLS4326, where CNS signs were traced to hybridization-independent AMPA receptor antagonism - but note that this was seen in NHP and mice and NOT in humans. RESTATES PRIMARY ROWS: the systemic stratum overlaps inotersen, patisiran, inclisiran and other agents already held in this dataset. grade_provisional

measurements.source_table: Figure 7B panels BI (overall AE prevalence by clinical AE group after intrathecal administration) and BII (severe AE prevalence in the same categories), with the Results subsection 'Cross-compartment AE patterns suggest limited peripheral toxicity after i.t. delivery and limited CNS toxicity after systemic delivery'
measurements.notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] GRADE 0 CROSS-COMPARTMENT ROW, the mirror image of TMP_dca_m7. is_cns_specific=FALSE because although the route is intrathecal the readout is deliberately taken OUTSIDE the CNS compartment - the second FALSE case the schema names, a CNS-delivered oligonucleotide whose readout is peripheral. Paper states verbatim: 'Among IT-administered treatments, non-neurologic AEs were observed across multiple clinical categories (Figure 7BI). However, the majority of these events were procedure-related or nonspecific in nature (e.g., general or mortality categories), and many are plausibly attributable to the underlying disease context or the invasive administration procedure itself. When analyses were restricted to SAEs, the representation of non-neurologic systemic categories was further reduced (Figure 7BII), suggesting that clinically significant peripheral toxicity following i.t. delivery is uncommon within the present dataset.' readout_value=TBD - Figure 7B is a prevalence plot with no printed values or denominators. USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT FROM THE DISCUSSION, which qualifies this negative: the authors note that 'multiple clinical pharmacokinetic analyses and regulatory reviews demonstrate measurable transfer of IT-dosed ASOs from the CSF to systemic circulation, with plasma exposure reflecting CSF clearance pathways rather than targeted peripheral distribution. Consequently, non-CNS related AEs remain relevant, even though overall systemic toxicity risk is lower than with systemic (SC/IV) dosing.' So this row supports 'low peripheral toxicity after IT dosing', not 'no peripheral exposure after IT dosing'. RESTATES PRIMARY ROWS: the intrathecal stratum is dominated by nusinersen, tofersen and tominersen, all already held from primary sources. grade_provisional

measurements.source_table: Figure 8B (heatmap, mean proportion of total observed AEs by AE category within each clinical indication), with the Results subsection 'AE distribution by clinical indication'
measurements.notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] CONFOUNDER ROW, filed so the confound is visible to a modeller rather than buried. Paper states verbatim: 'For example, neurologic AEs were most prominent in neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental indications, consistent with the underlying disease context' and treats this as an internal-consistency check: 'These findings support the internal consistency of the curated dataset and indicate that AE patterns generally correspond to the treated disease category.' GRADED 0 DELIBERATELY: the authors attribute the neurologic AE excess in these indications to the underlying disease, not to the oligonucleotide, so no drug-attributable CNS signal is demonstrated and the rubric's grade-0 definition applies. is_cns_specific=FALSE for the same reason - this is a property of the indication mix, not a CNS-compartment measurement. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT IN THE WHOLE ATLAS FOR CNS WORK, and it applies to every SafeSense row in this lane: intrathecally delivered ASOs are given almost exclusively to patients with severe neurologic disease, so route, indication and disease severity are collinear by construction. The authors say so plainly: 'SafeSense also does not fully separate ASO-associated AEs from procedure-related events or manifestations of the underlying disease... We therefore interpret these patterns as reflecting an indication - ASO interaction rather than isolated drug toxicity alone. Systematic placebo-based or natural-history correction was not feasible because many sources lacked appropriate comparator groups.' Any model that uses the SafeSense structure-toxicity rows (TMP_dca_m3/m4/m5) as CNS toxicity labels without conditioning on indication will recover disease severity, not chemistry. grade_provisional

=== TARGET 1 - NUSINERSEN DOSE CONTRAST: THE PREMISE IS PARTLY WRONG, AND THIS MATTERS ===
The two denominators in the brief are exactly right, but three structural assumptions behind them are not, and a reviewer must not use these tables as a clean within-oligo dose-response contrast.

VERIFIED TABLE NUMBERS (label sec 6.1, version 21):
- Table 2, Study 1 (NCT02193074, infantile-onset), SPINRAZA 12 mg N=80 vs Sham-Procedure Control N=41. All 8 rows, SPINRAZA% / sham%: Lower respiratory infection 55/37, Constipation 35/22, Teething 18/7, Urinary tract infection 9/0, Upper respiratory tract congestion 8/2, Ear infection 6/2, Flatulence 5/2, Decreased weight 5/2.
- Table 3, Study 2 (NCT02292537, later-onset), SPINRAZA 12 mg N=84 vs Sham-Procedure Control N=42. All 8 rows: Pyrexia 43/36, Headache 29/7, Vomiting 29/12, Back pain 25/0, Epistaxis 7/0, Fall 5/0, Respiratory tract congestion 5/2, Seasonal allergy 5/2.
- Table 4, Study 4 (NCT04089566 DEVOTE Part B, infantile-onset), SPINRAZA High Dose Regimen N=50 vs Matched Sham Control (Study 1) N=20. All 7 rows: Pneumonia 20/5, COVID-19 16/0, Pneumonia aspiration 14/5, Malnutrition 10/0, Procedural pain 6/0, Myocardial necrosis marker increased 6/0, Anemia 6/0.
There are exactly three adverse-reaction tables in the label (verified by enumerating all 8 table captions); Table 4 is the ONLY high-dose AE table. The later-onset high-dose cohort in Study 4 (n=16 high dose vs n=8 low dose) got no adverse-reaction table at all.

CORRECTION 1 - THE HIGH-DOSE COMPARATOR IS NOT CONCURRENT. The brief says each dose level has 'its own concurrent sham control'. It does not. Label sec 6.1 says verbatim that the comparison is against 'historic-matched sham-control patients from Study 1', and the Table 4 header reads 'Matched Sham Control (Study 1)'. Study 1 is the 12 mg trial. So the N=20 high-dose comparator is a matched SUBSET of the N=41 comparator used for the 12 mg table: the two control groups are NESTED, not independent, and the high-dose comparison is externally controlled. The label itself flags the populations are not exchangeable - sec 14.1 notes Study 4 patients 'had shorter disease duration... and lower baseline CHOP-INTEND scores, suggesting they were progressing more' rapidly than the Study 1 infantile-onset population.

CORRECTION 2 - THE TABLES ARE THRESHOLD-FILTERED, SO ABSENCE IS NOT ZERO. Every table lists only reactions occurring in at least 5% of SPINRAZA patients AND at least 5% more frequently or at least 2 times as frequently as control. An event missing from a table has an unknown incidence below that bar, not an incidence of zero. With N=50 in Table 4 one patient is 2%, so events affecting fewer than about 3 patients could not appear at all. No dose-response ratio may be computed across the two tables from listed-vs-unlisted status.

CORRECTION 3 - AND THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL - THE LABEL TABLES CONTAIN ALMOST NO CNS EVENTS. Table 2 (12 mg, N=80/41) contains ZERO neurologic or CNS terms; all eight entries are infectious, gastrointestinal, dental or growth terms. Table 4 (high dose, N=50/20) contains exactly ONE neurologic or procedure-related term, Procedural pain 6% vs 0%. So the clean same-molecule, same-route, two-dose CNS contrast the brief hoped for does not exist in this label. The neurologic terms - headache 29/7, back pain 25/0, fall 5/0 - live only in Table 3, which is the later-onset 12 mg table (N=84 vs 42) and has NO high-dose counterpart. The two tables the brief names cannot be paired on any neurologic endpoint except procedural pain, and even that pairing is one-sided because Table 2 does not list it.

WHAT I FILED FOR TARGET 1: 2 rows, not the larger set the brief anticipated, because only 2 exist. TMP_dca_m1 = Procedural pain 6% vs 0% at the High Dose Regimen (implied 3/50 vs 0/20; counts are arithmetic from printed percentages, flagged as implied since the label prints percentages only). TMP_dca_m2 = a grade-0 negative anchor recording that no CNS term met the reporting threshold anywhere in Table 4, with all seven rows transcribed into notes.

SHAM COMPARATOR CAVEAT, APPLIED AS INSTRUCTED: the sham procedure in Studies 1 and 2 is a skin prick with no dural puncture, so procedure-attributable events (procedural pain, post-lumbar-puncture headache, back pain) are systematically exaggerated - only the treated arm was actually punctured. Procedural pain is therefore graded 1, not 2, and the caveat is written into the row's notes. No event at or below its sham rate was filed above grade 0.

=== WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT FILE FOR TARGET 1 (already in the dataset, verified rather than duplicated) ===
I re-verified these against label version 21 instead of re-filing them, to avoid inflating the row count with duplicates:
- Table 2's negative is ALREADY CMS1175, whose notes list the same eight terms with the same percentages and the same N=80/41. Still exact against v21. Nothing new to add.
- Table 3's neurologic rows are ALREADY CMS1176 (back pain 25 vs 0), CMS1178 (headache 29 vs 7), CMS1179 (vomiting 29 vs 12), CMS1177 (fall 5 vs 0), with denominators 84/42 recorded in their notes. All four still match version 21 EXACTLY - no value has changed in the high-dose revision. Treat this as a positive verification result for those rows.
- The juvenile-monkey safety margin in sec 8.4 - 'The no-effect dose for neurohistopathology in monkeys (0.3 mg/dose) is approximately equivalent to and lower than the recommended clinical maintenance doses of 12 and 28 mg, respectively' - is ALREADY quoted verbatim in the notes of CMS1186. Worth a reviewer's attention on its own merits (the animal no-effect dose for hippocampal neuronal vacuolation and necrosis is at the 12 mg clinical dose and BELOW the newly approved 28 mg maintenance dose, i.e. the high-dose regimen has no margin to the animal neurohistopathology NOEL), but it is not new to the dataset and I did not create a second row for it.
- Non-CNS dose contrasts in the new label that this dataset does not cover and that I did not file because they are out of CNS scope: immunogenicity, Low Dose Regimen 38/367 (10%) treatment-emergent ADAs vs High Dose Regimen 11/117 (9%) (sec 12.6); cardiac QTcF >500 ms or change >60 ms in 4/247 (2.4%) (sec 12.2); thrombocytopenia 24/146 (16%) SPINRAZA vs 10/72 (14%) sham and elevated urine protein 71/123 (58%) vs 22/65 (34%) (sec 5.1, 5.2). === TARGET 2 - SAFESENSE: RESOLVED, REAL, BUT NOT CC-BY ===
IDENTIFIER CONFIRMED. DOI 10.1016/j.omtn.2026.103035 resolves (via doi.org to linkinghub.elsevier.com PII S2162253126002064). CrossRef confirms the title, journal (Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids), volume 37, issue 3, article 103035, and all seven authors exactly as given in the brief: Noam Vaknin, Aviv Ziv, Tom Chernobylsky, Sharon Avkin-Nachum, Gideon Rechavi, Dan Dominissini, Nofar Mor. PMID 42633286, PMC13499347. CrossRef gives the issue date as 2026-09 with the version-of-record licence starting 2026-07-21; the brief's '2026' is right.

LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, therefore redistribution=summary_stat on every SafeSense row, exactly as the brief directed for an NC or ND licence. This was checked in BOTH places: the PMC permissions block reads verbatim '(c) 2026 The Author(s) ... https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/ This is an open access article under the CC BY-NC-ND license', and CrossRef independently reports content-version 'vor' under http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/. The PMC record also carries the property pmc-license-ref 'CC BY-NC-ND'. It is open access but NOT cc_by - the ND term in particular would be violated by republishing their harmonized tables inside a CC-BY dataset.

SCALE (all read from the Results text): 41,730 treated patients, 112 ASO treatments, 42,092 AEs, 1,734 distinct AE terms, 7,072 (16.8%) severe. AEs reported for 87 treatments, 58 with documented severe AEs. 616 records included from 3,396 identified; 246 sources gave evaluable safety data. Last updated February 2026. The brief's expectation that this is the largest structured collection of human ASO AEs is consistent with what the paper claims.

THE CENTRAL DISAPPOINTMENT, STATED PLAINLY: SafeSense publishes ALMOST NO NUMBERS AT OUR GRAIN. Its CNS content is delivered entirely as radar plots, WLS coefficient plots, scatterplots and heatmaps (Figures 4B, 5A/5B, 6C, 7B/7C, 8B). Not one neurologic AE rate, numerator or per-category denominator is printed in the text, and the supplementary tables do not supply them either - S1 is a list of source references, S2 the canonical AE dictionary, S3 the ASO metadata. The only per-comparison statistics printed anywhere in the text are two p-values, both non-neurologic (i.v. vs s.c. severe AEs p=0.04383; severe haematologic AEs p=0.01401); Figure 5B significance is given only as asterisk bands. The per-ASO 'gold table' that holds the counts lives in the Streamlit portal, which I could not fetch (see FAILED TO FETCH above). Consequently EVERY SafeSense row I filed carries readout_value=TBD, with the reason recorded in the row. I chose to file them with TBD rather than transcribe magnitudes off figures by eye, which the contract forbids. If the portal can be reached, this lane should be re-run - that is where the extractable numbers are.

WHAT I FILED FOR TARGET 2: 7 rows (TMP_dca_m3 through m9), ALL class-level, on a single class_review oligo. Three structure-toxicity associations with a neurologic component (gapmer vs fully-modified, LNA vs 2'-MOE, PO/PS vs PS-only), all graded 1 - deliberately not 2, because an aggregate AE-category rate with no severity-resolved CNS event definition, no injury biomarker and no imaging does not meet the rubric's grade-2 band. Four grade-0 null or negative rows (length not associated with AE burden; neurologic AEs after systemic dosing are nonspecific; non-neurologic AEs after intrathecal dosing are mostly procedural; neurologic AE share tracks indication).

DOUBLE-COUNTING - HOW I HANDLED IT. I filed NO per-oligo AE rate from SafeSense. Every nusinersen, tofersen, tominersen, milasen or valeriasen number in that atlas is an aggregation of clinical trial records, labels, publications and FAERS reports - the same primary sources this dataset already holds directly (nusinersen 97 rows, tofersen 146, tominersen 150, plus milasen at CNS010/CNS287 and valeriasen at CNS286). Filing any of them would have re-entered the same patients under a second source_id, and the assembler cannot detect that. What I filed instead is only the cross-programme associations, which are genuinely additive because no primary row in this dataset computes them. But they are still derived from overlapping patients, so: THE SEVEN SAFESENSE ROWS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE AND THEIR PATIENT COUNTS MUST NEVER BE ADDED TO THE PER-OLIGO ROWS. Every one of the seven says so in its own notes field, as the brief required. The nusinersen overlap is the most severe: the paper itself states nusinersen 'accounts for a substantial proportion of treated participants and is concentrated within the FM, 2'-MOE, and i.t. strata', which is precisely the stratum this dataset is densest in.

A SECOND, SUBTLER DOUBLE-COUNTING RISK INSIDE TARGET 1. Label Study 4 is NCT04089566 (DEVOTE) Part B. Its n=50 infantile-onset high-dose patients are the SAME 50 patients already represented by CMS1304 (acquired macrocephaly 1/50, from the NCT04089566 posted results) and by CMS1589, CMS1597, CMS1600 and CMS1603 (from the DEVOTE paper doi:10.1038/s41591-025-04193-6). TMP_dca_m1 and m2 add a new endpoint on that cohort, not new patients. Both rows carry the warning.

=== ONE THING A REVIEWER SHOULD KNOW ABOUT SAFESENSE'S OWN METHOD ===
The atlas was assembled with heavy LLM assistance - the Methods name ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Perplexity and OpenEvidence as retrieval and extraction tools used between January 2025 and February 2026. The authors state that AI was used 'solely for information discovery, structured data extraction, cross-source comparison, and preliminary summarization', that it was 'not used for analytical decision-making or interpretation', and that 'All candidate records underwent mandatory manual validation prior to database inclusion... independently verified against primary source documents by domain-expert researchers.' That is a reasonable disclosure and I am not asserting the data are wrong. But since this dataset may itself be used to train or benchmark models, a downstream consumer should know that the SafeSense rows are second-order machine-assisted extractions with human validation, whereas the label rows in this lane are first-order transcriptions from a regulatory document. They should not be weighted equally.
